title: All three NFL Thanksgiving games decided in the final three seconds
excerpt: The Bears, Eagles and Bills all won at the death, with Philadelphia completing the biggest comeback in Thanksgiving history.
content_html:
All three NFL games played on Thanksgiving Day in the United States were decided in the last three seconds, capped by the largest comeback in the holiday's history.

Bears 39, Lions 35

Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams threw a six-yard touchdown pass to Rome Odunze with three seconds left to win a high-scoring NFC North contest in Detroit.

Eagles 39, Cowboys 38

Dallas led 31-10 in the second half and lost. Philadelphia wiped out the 21-point deficit, the biggest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history, and kicker Jake Elliott won it with a 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining.

Bills 13, Chiefs 10

The night game in Orchard Park was a grind played in cold, wet and windy conditions. It seemed headed for overtime until a Kansas City three-and-out and a deflected punt handed Buffalo good field position. Greg Dortch returned the punt 15 yards, and Tyler Bass kicked a 57-yard field goal as time expired.

Kansas City will rue a missed 46-yard attempt by Harrison Butker earlier in the game. The defeat leaves the Chiefs at 8-3.

A new night on the calendar

The holiday week started a day early. In the league's first Thanksgiving Eve game, streamed on Netflix, the Los Angeles Rams beat the Green Bay Packers 26-13. Blake Corum ran for a career-best 184 yards on 32 carries as the Rams out-rushed Green Bay 241 yards to 55. It was the Rams' fifth straight win and lifted them to 7-4.

The week closed on Friday with the fourth annual Black Friday game. Pittsburgh beat Denver 27-5, two days after releasing quarterback Aaron Rodgers, ending the Broncos' six-game winning streak. According to CBS Sports, no NFL game had finished with that score before.

A growing tradition

Thanksgiving football has expanded steadily. Detroit has hosted a holiday game since 1934 and Dallas joined in 1966. A third game was added in 2006, Black Friday arrived in 2023, and the Thanksgiving Eve game is new this year. Last year's games were also full of surprises: Green Bay, Dallas and Cincinnati all won as underdogs.

A bigger holiday footprint

Five games in three days, spread across free-to-air television, Netflix and Amazon Prime Video, show the league's push to own whole holidays rather than single time slots. A Christmas Day triple-header is next.
